description: A bright yellow Taraxacum japonicum, the common dandelion of Japan's fields and roadsides.
A big, ruffled Chinese peony in pink and white, the flower of the Luoyang gardens.
A shining yellow spring flower of Manchuria and Japan that blooms through the last of the snow.
An orange Lilium lancifolium with dark freckles, native to eastern China and Japan.
A tall spike of magenta flowers, the first colour to return to burned ground across Kamchatka.  Its seeds are good food.
A star-shaped blue-violet Platycodon grandiflorus, long grown in China and Japan.
A yellow arctic poppy of the Kamchatka tundra, changed into something stranger.
A fat bush of crimson Rosa rugosa, the beach rose of Japan and the Russian Far East.  Watch out for its thorns.
A wide bush of pale pinkish-purple Syringa, native to Manchuria and northern China.
The top of a fireweed stalk, with magenta petals and some seeds that have yet to be eaten by animals.
A bud of the Kamchatka poppy.  Contains some substances commonly produced by a mutated poppy flower.
A mixed bunch of chrysanthemums, peonies and bellflowers.  Unfortunately, they have all withered with time.
